text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Air France chairman Christian Blanc defuses a planned pilots' strike by threatening to resign if strike went ahead, finds a compromise on wages.
-- Financial markets expect a rise in U.S. interest rates.
-- Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet expected to propose merger with Lyonnaise des Eaux at an April 1 board meeting. Shareholders Axa-UAP, Saint-Gobain and Credit Agricole seen backig the move.
-- Leaders of small and medium-sized French companies more optimistic, consider new investment, paper's survey shows.
-- Investors come back to European equity markets.
-- L'Oreal chairman Lindsay Owen-Jones says in an interview he has set a 100-billion-franc turnover target for 2001.
-- PSA Peugeot Citroen to invest in an assembly plant in Brasil, and unveil an agreement with workers this week, according to chairman Jacques Calvet.
-- According to a World Bank report issued yesterday, private capital flows to developing countries increased by 60 biliion dollars in 1996 to reach 244 billion dollars.
-- Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux may consider merger.
